document.title: Afghanistan: A Report of Pakistani Military Assistance to the Taliban
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] Relays an unconfirmed incident of alleged Pakistani military assistance: 25 large Mercedes Benz trucks full of Pakistani fighters delivered to Kabul airport for transport to Kunduz to assist the Taliban.

persons.role: Principal Officer, American Consulate Peshawar (classifier and signatory of the cable)

events.description: A convoy of 25 covered Mercedes Benz trucks, said to carry about 2000 Pakistani fighters, travelled at night from Jalalabad to Kabul airport, probably for onward transport to Kunduz. The report is unverified.
The Afghan political contact (name redacted) told a consulate officer of the truck driver's account.
A particularly large influx of Pakistani Taliban joined the Taliban in summer 1997.
Consulate Peshawar sent the cable reporting alleged Pakistani military assistance to the Taliban.
A particularly large influx of Pakistani Taliban joined the Taliban in summer 1997.
25 Mercedes trucks reportedly carried about 2000 alleged Pakistani fighters at night from Jalalabad to Kabul airport for probable onward transport to Kunduz.
An Afghan political contact told the Peshawar consulate principal officer about the alleged transport.
The consulate cable reporting alleged Pakistani military assistance to the Taliban was sent.

key_claims: An Afghan political contact reported that about 2000 alleged Pakistani fighters were trucked from Jalalabad to Kabul airport around 8 March 1998, bound for Kunduz.
The consulate could not independently verify the report and judged the 2000 figure high for 25 trucks.
The Afghan contact implied that some part of the Pakistani government assisted the operation, given its scale and organization.
Hundreds of Pakistani madrassah Taliban joined the Taliban, with a particularly large influx in summer 1997.
The consulate had earlier reported anecdotal evidence of Pakistani military and intelligence officers advising the Taliban inside Afghanistan.
If true, the incident would be a major escalation of Pakistani assistance ahead of a third Taliban northern offensive in spring 1998.
